stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab: DoT, telcos push telecom restoration in cyclone-hit Andhra, Odisha
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: DoT, telcos push telecom restoration in cyclone-hit Andhra, Odisha
stories.summary: Commercial power supply disruptions and localised optical fibre cable cuts remain the main hurdles
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The government, in coordination with telcos, is undertaking restoration efforts and monitoring the telecom network situation to ensure the continuity of essential communication services in the affected areas, after Cyclone Arnab hit along the coast of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, an official release said on Friday.
Heavy rain, flash floods, fallen trees and power disruptions had hit services in parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and adjoining regions, it said.
Telecom restoration efforts are underway in affected districts through coordinated action with service providers, the Telecom Department said in a release.

Emergency connectivity arrangements, including Intra-Circle Roaming (ICR) and Cell on Wheel deployments, are being maintained to facilitate uninterrupted communication for citizens and support relief and restoration activities in the affected regions, it said.
In Andhra Pradesh, overall network availability has reached 99.18 per cent.
Among affected districts, availability stands at 98.5 per cent in West Godavari and 91.96 per cent in Dr B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema.
Commercial power supply disruptions and localised optical fibre cable cuts remain the main hurdles.

Intra-Circle Roaming (ICR) is operational across affected districts, letting subscribers connect irrespective of their service provider, and 11 Cell on Wheels units have been deployed for emergency communication.
In Odisha, the situation in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts is gradually improving as rain eases and floodwaters recede.

All telcos are making sustained efforts on a priority basis to restore the remaining affected sites and ensure early normalisation of telecom services and uninterrupted connectivity for the public, the release added.

stories.headline: Missing woman in J-K suspected to have crossed LoC into Pakistan
stories.title: Missing woman in J-K suspected to have crossed LoC into Pakistan
stories.summary: Jammu, Oct 31: A woman has gone missing in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch district and is suspected to have crossed the Line of Control (LoC) into Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) along with eight goats, officials said on Saturday. Rubina Kousar, a resident of Karni village near the LoC, took the goats out for grazing on Friday but did not return home by evening, they said. They said preliminary information suggests that she may have crossed the LoC into Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) along with the livestock. It was not immediately clear whether she crossed the LoC inadvertently while grazing the goats or did so deliberately, they added. Several families living along the LoC have relatives across the divide in PoK, making it difficult to ascertain the circumstances behind her suspected crossing, officials said. Further details are awaited.

stories.headline: Power bills enter the US election fight
stories.title: Power bills enter the US election fight
stories.summary: New York: US electricity prices had flown under the radar in past national elections, but they have become a major political issue in this year's midterms as Americans grow angry over rising utility bills and deals for power-hungry data centers.Nationwide, according to Energy Information Administration data, electricity prices for homes have risen more than 10% since 2024 when President Donald Trump was elected along with Republican majorities in both houses of the US Congress. Higher electricity prices have outpaced the rise in costs for other goods and services.Also Read: US midterms may raise shutdown, debt risks; keep tariff uncertainty high: ICICI BankPower bills have grown even faster in political battleground states of Ohio, Michigan and Pennsylvania, which are also hot spots for new data centers. In some cases, electricity bills have soared by triple the inflation rate.Many politicians vying for top statehouse seats across the country this year have backed cracking down on utilities. Some have proposed freezing utility rate increases and slashing guaranteed returns, steps that could have sweeping consequences for the country's utility industry."It could be the first election to feature utilities and electricity, specifically, as a prominent issue in the midterms," said Charles Hua, executive director of PowerLines, a nonprofit that advocates reforming utility policy to favor consumers. "Part of that is because people's utility bills have gone up and up, and they don't see any end in sight."Utilities are heavily regulated. State regulators generally must approve utilities' requests to spend on the grid and to recover those costs through rate increases. Regulators also set the return on equity utilities can earn on their grid investments.This year, utilities are on track to match last year's record high $31 billion in rate increase requests to regulators, a PowerLines survey showed. Last year's spending was double the previous record.The investor-owned companies are also expected to carry out a record of nearly $1.3 trillion in capital spending over the next five years, according to an analysis by S&P Global's Regulatory Research Associates.UTILITIES SPOTLIGHTEDSeats on nine state public utility commissions are up for election this year, nearly all the US states where voters elect their utility regulators. These include burgeoning data center hubs Arizona and Georgia.Governors will be chosen in 36 US states this year, and governors appoint utility regulators in states where commissioners are not directly elected.Also Read: Dishing dosas to hopping temples: US midterm poll candidates reach out to Indian AmericansIn Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton has promised to lower energy bills if she is elected governor. Her campaign said she will also appoint a public utilities commission that was "not beholden to utility companies" and work with the state attorney general to crack down on "excessive rate hikes and predatory practices."Ohio's residential electricity bills have grown by more than 20% over the last two years, according to EIA data.Acton has also said she supports a data center moratorium. Her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy said he would assure Ohioans living near data centers would not pay electricity bills at all.BULLY PULPITSome governors who are up for reelection have used their political weight to pressure the power industry to keep prices down.In April, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro announced that prominent utility, PECO Energy Company, had acceded to his demand that it withdraw its proposal with state regulators to increase rates. She did so the same day she took office.In Virginia, home to the largest concentration of data centers in the world, Governor Abigail Spanberger took a similar approach, which industry analysts said could offer a playbook for those who win this year's elections.Utility advocates say reducing guaranteed returns and freezing rates will not make a meaningful difference in household bills but could lead to a long-term reduction of investments in the grid."The grid is America's greatest machine, and it doesn't operate on the political calendar," said Drew Maloney, president of Edison Electric Institute, a trade organization for investor-owned electric utilities. "It requires consistent investment every year to deliver reliable energy to our customers."Credit rating agency Fitch downgraded the North American utility sector to "deteriorating" from "neutral" in June, citing political pressure in the midterms to limit electricity bills and utility profits.For an industry that plans in decades, it is hard to predict the result of short-term political moves aimed at saving money for households."I do think the real meat will come after the election," Hua said.

Power bills have grown even faster in political battleground states of Ohio, Michigan and Pennsylvania, which are also hot spots for new data centers.
In some cases, electricity bills have soared by triple the inflation rate.
Many politicians vying for top statehouse seats across the country this year have backed cracking down on utilities.

Some have proposed freezing utility rate increases and slashing guaranteed returns, steps that could have sweeping consequences for the country's utility industry." It could be the first election to feature utilities and electricity, specifically, as a prominent issue in the midterms," said Charles Hua, executive director of PowerLines, a nonprofit that advocates reforming utility policy to favor consumers.
"Part of that is because people's utility bills have gone up and up, and they don't see any end in sight." Utilities are heavily regulated.
State regulators generally must approve utilities' requests to spend on the grid and to recover those costs through rate increases.
Regulators also set the return on equity utilities can earn on their grid investments.
This year, utilities are on track to match last year's record high $31 billion in rate increase requests to regulators, a PowerLines survey showed.
Last year's spending was double the previous record.
UTILITIES SPOTLIGHTEDSeats on nine state public utility commissions are up for election this year, nearly all the US states where voters elect their utility regulators.
These include burgeoning data center hubs Arizona and Georgia.
Governors will be chosen in 36 US states this year, and governors appoint utility regulators in states where commissioners are not directly elected.
In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton has promised to lower energy bills if she is elected governor.
Acton has also said she supports a data center moratorium.
Her Republican opponent.
Vivek Ramaswamy said he would assure Ohioans living near data centers would not pay electricity bills at all.

In April, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro announced that prominent utility, PECO Energy Company, had acceded to his demand that it withdraw its proposal with state regulators to increase rates.
Shapiro, a Democrat running for reelection, said the move would reduce future utility bills by as much as $34 a month.

He followed up with a letter to more utility CEOs seeking changes in how utilities justify spending and returns on equity." The governors are using this crisis on energy affordability as an opportunity to take a deeper dive into the utility regulatory model and see if it makes any sense," said Jamie Van Nostrand, senior fellow at the Kleinman Center for Energy Policy at the University of Pennsylvania and former chair of the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities.

Power bills tracked low inflation for roughly a decade, and were not an issue in most mainstream elections until last year, when Mikie Sherrill successfully ran for New Jersey governor on the promise of freezing utility bills.
She did so the same day she took office.

In Virginia, home to the largest concentration of data centers in the world, Governor Abigail Spanberger took a similar approach, which industry analysts said could offer a playbook for those who win this year's elections.

Utility advocates say reducing guaranteed returns and freezing rates will not make a meaningful difference in household bills but could lead to a long-term reduction of investments in the grid." The grid is America's greatest machine, and it doesn't operate on the political calendar," said Drew Maloney, president of Edison Electric Institute, a trade organization for investor-owned electric utilities.

"It requires consistent investment every year to deliver reliable energy to our customers." Credit rating agency Fitch downgraded the North American utility sector to "deteriorating" from "neutral" in June, citing political pressure in the midterms to limit electricity bills and utility profits.

For an industry that plans in decades, it is hard to predict the result of short-term political moves aimed at saving money for households." I do think the real meat will come after the election," Hua said.

stories.headline: IPS officer who led Pahalgam attack probe bags Home Minister’s medal
stories.title: IPS officer who led Pahalgam attack probe bags Home Minister’s medal
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 31: IPS officer Sandeep Chaudhary, a 2012-batch officer who headed the investigation into the Pahalgam terror attack, has been awarded the ‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ for outstanding work in investigation. The medal is among the awards conferred on 490 personnel from various States, Union Territories, Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Central Police Organisations (CPOs) for the year 2026, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). The Ministry said the medal recognises excellent work, promotes high professional standards and boosts the morale of police and other personnel. “The award was instituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs through a notification dated February 1, 2024, and is conferred on personnel of police forces, security organisations, intelligence wings, CAPFs, CPOs, the National Security Guard, Assam Rifles and forensic science departments for excellence in operations, outstanding investigation, exceptional performance, intelligence services and meritorious work in forensic science,” the Ministry said. The medal is announced every year on October 31 to mark the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.—(KNO)

stories.headline: IAF bids farewell to Air Chief Marshal Singh after 42 years
stories.title: IAF bids farewell to Air Chief Marshal Singh after 42 years
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 31 : Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh bid farewell to the Indian Air Force (IAF) after 42 years of military service on Saturday. Earlier in the day, Air Chief Marshal Singh, who led the IAF during 'Operation Sindoor', laid a wreath at the National War Memorial to honour the memory of those who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty. Air Chief Marshal Singh was then accorded a ceremonial Guard of Honour at the Parade Ground of the Air Force Station ahead of the handover of the command to Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who took over as the new Chief of the Air Staff on Saturday. An accomplished fighter pilot and an Experimental Test Pilot, Air Chief Marshal Singh has made significant contributions to the operational capability, combat preparedness and modernisation of the IAF. "His tenure as the Chief of the Air Staff was marked by decisive leadership and an unwavering focus on operational readiness, particularly during Operation SINDOOR, wherein the Indian Air Force demonstrated its combat capability, operational precision and resolve in the service of national objectives. His leadership reinforced the IAF's ability to respond decisively across the full spectrum of operations," the IAF said in a statement. Beyond operational leadership, Air Chief Marshal Singh will be remembered for his "deep and personal connect with air warriors across the length and breadth of the organisation", the force said, adding, "His interactions with personnel at the grassroots level reflected his conviction that the strength of the Indian Air Force rests in its people." "Whether engaging with the last air warrior in the chain of command or interacting with young officers, airmen and cadets, he consistently emphasised professionalism, accountability, initiative and pride in service. His ability to connect with young minds and inspire confidence reflected his belief in nurturing the next generation of air warriors and leaders," the IAF said. Throughout his tenure, he focussed on creating a technologically empowered and future-ready IAF, with emphasis on indigenisation, innovation and the integration of emerging technologies. "His vision and guidance have further strengthened the organisation's resolve towards building a capable, credible and combat-ready force," the IAF said. The force further wished Air Chief Marshal Singh and his wife Sarita Singh the "very best for the years ahead". "His legacy of leadership, operational resolve and enduring connect with air warriors will continue to inspire generations," the force said. Earlier, President Droupadi Murmu and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh bid a warm farewell to Air Chief Marshal Singh, commending his "distinguished service, exemplary leadership and invaluable contributions to the Indian Air Force and the nation". Defence Minister Singh acknowledged the key role played by the former IAF chief during the successful execution of 'Operation Sindoor'. --IANS

stories.headline: Rupee seen as India's first line of defence against energy shocks: IMF
stories.title: Rupee seen as India's first line of defence against energy shocks: IMF
stories.summary: Washington, Oct 31 : The International Monetary Fund has said the rupee should be India’s “first line of defense” against the energy shock from the war in the Middle East, signalling a preference for exchange rate flexibility over heavy central bank intervention, even as it kept its 7 per cent growth forecast for the Indian economy. Responding to a question at her regular press briefing in Washington on Thursday about the Reserve Bank of India’s recent intervention to support the rupee, IMF Communications Director Julie Kozack said she was echoing the head of the Fund’s Asia and Pacific Department, Krishna Srinivasan. “Given the ongoing energy shocks that India is confronting, like all countries, our view is that the rupee should be the first line of defense in the face of these shocks,” Kozack said. “So, allowing the exchange rate to move freely to reflect the impact of these shocks is important to help the Indian economy adjust to these shocks,” she said. Kozack said the Fund’s advice would change if a weaker currency started to push up prices across the economy. “If significant rupee depreciation leads to broad-based increases in inflation, then our advice would be that monetary policy tightening could be considered to preserve price stability,” she said. She did not rule out intervention altogether. “And more generally, foreign exchange intervention can be appropriate when market conditions become disorderly,” Kozack said, adding that this would be consistent with the IMF’s Integrated Policy Framework. “But in the case of India, our view is that exchange rate flexibility remains the preferable policy response,” she said. On growth, Kozack described India as “really an engine of growth in the world economy.” “We do project growth in India at 7 percent both for FY 2026-2027 and FY 2027-2028,” she said, citing robust domestic demand and strong services activity. “So, India right now has quite a lot of growth momentum,” she added. She flagged the weather as the main downside risk. Worse-than-expected weather, “including because of an El Niño, could lower crop yields in India, and it could kind of weigh on activity, particularly in rural areas,” Kozack said, adding that it could also lead to higher food price inflation and hurt household purchasing power. “Right now those risks have not materialized,” she said. The Fund will next reassess its India projections in its January World Economic Outlook update. Kozack also said financial conditions for emerging economies remained broadly supportive despite higher bond yields. “Spreads in emerging and developing countries are still quite compressed,” she said, attributing it to years of work by those countries to strengthen their fundamentals. On the United States, she said the Federal Reserve under Chairman Kevin Warsh was “appropriately remaining data-dependent” after holding rates on Wednesday following a hike in September, and that headline US inflation remained above the Fed’s 2 per cent target, partly because of the energy price shock from the Middle East war. Asked about the US Treasury’s October 14 statement calling on the Fund to sharpen its work on global imbalances and debt sustainability, Kozack said the United States was the IMF’s largest shareholder and that “we do value the voice and engagement of the United States.” She referred questions on the meaning of the statement to the Treasury. --IANS

Asked about the US Treasury’s October 14 statement calling on the Fund to sharpen its work on global imbalances and debt sustainability, Kozack said the United States was the IMF’s largest shareholder and that “we do value the voice and engagement of the United States.” She referred questions on the meaning of the statement to the Treasury.
--IANS.

stories.headline: Congress pays tribute to Indira Gandhi and her enduring legacy
stories.title: Congress pays tribute to Indira Gandhi and her enduring legacy
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 31 : The Congress party paid homage to former Prime Minister late Indira Gandhi on her death anniversary at the Shakti Sthal in New Delhi on Saturday. Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) Chairperson Sonia Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress National President Mallikarjun Kharge, Congress General Secretary K.C. Venugopal and several other party leaders arrived at the Shakti Sthal to pay floral tributes to the former Prime Minister. Earlier, Congress took to X and posted, "On the death anniversary of India's first woman Prime Minister, a symbol of indomitable courage and willpower, Smt. Indira Gandhi ji, humble tribute." "We remember her courage, strong leadership and lifelong commitment to India's unity, integrity and progress," the party said in another post. Indira Gandhi, popularly known as the 'Iron Lady of India,' was born on November 19, 1917, in Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh, into a Kashmiri Pandit family. She was the daughter of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Kamala Nehru. National Integration Day, observed annually on November 19, coincides with Gandhi's birth anniversary and serves to honour her pivotal role in shaping India's political, social, and economic journey. As India progresses toward becoming a global power, National Integration Day acts as a reminder of Gandhi's contributions to unifying the nation. The observance was instituted by the Indian National Congress in 1985 to commemorate her efforts in promoting unity. The day holds deep significance, serving as an opportunity to celebrate India's diversity and recognise the importance of collective efforts for the country's development. During her tenure as Prime Minister from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 until her tragic assassination in 1984, Gandhi worked relentlessly to strengthen national integration. Her political career was defined by her unwavering commitment to unity and integrity. One of her landmark achievements was her decisive leadership during the 1971 India-Pakistan war, which led to the creation of Bangladesh. Her actions solidified her reputation as a leader with a strong vision and resolve. --IANS

stories.headline: Badrinath-Dehradun Helicopter Crash: 6 Dead, Passenger’s Video Captures Moments Before Tragedy
stories.title: Badrinath-Dehradun Helicopter Crash: 6 Dead, Passenger’s Video Captures Moments Before Tragedy
stories.summary: A helicopter operated by Trans Bharat Aviation crashed in Joshimath, Uttarakhand's Chamoli district, while flying from Badrinath to Dehradun. All six people on board — the pilot and five passengers — were killed. One passenger, Pratap, had sent a video from inside the helicopter to his family shortly before the crash. The footage, intended to share his journey, has become a heartbreaking record of his final moments. The mortal remains of all six victims have been recovered. The Uttarakhand and Karnataka governments are coordinating their transportation to Bengaluru. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has dispatched a team for a preliminary assessment, while authorities have grounded Trans Bharat Aviation's entire fleet as a precaution. The crash has renewed concerns over helicopter safety on Uttarakhand's high-altitude pilgrimage routes.

stories.title: SEBI chairman says market regulator keeping eye on Tata Group developments
stories.summary: The comments came amid differences over governance matters at Tata Sons, the group's holding company, including the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman and the question of its proposed listing.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'market regulator' in title weight 40
article_sentences: The comments came amid differences over governance matters at Tata Sons, the group's holding company, including the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman and the question of its proposed listing.

SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Saturday said the market regulator is monitoring developments relating to governance at the holding company level in the Tata Group, and pointed out that the group's listed companies and their promoters are subject to SEBI's disclosure and compliance norms.
"At the holding company level, there are some issues, as that's not really a listed company.

The rest of the companies, those which are listed, follow all the LODR (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) norms," Pandey told reporters on the sidelines of the launch of the Bharat Chamber Investors Forum.
These listed companies and promoters of those firms are subject to all norms, he said.
Asked whether the SEBI was keeping track of Tata Group's developments, he said, "Yes...
I mean in the sense of, you know, we have to keep monitoring all the developments."
Pandey did not refer to any specific governance violation or regulatory action against the group in his remarks.
The Tata Group has 26 publicly listed companies, with a combined market capitalisation of $328 billion as of March 31, 2025, according to its FY25 annual report.
Of these, seven listed companies collectively hold around 11.92% in Tata Sons, according to an analysis by governance advisory firm InGovern.
The firms also have more than 1.77 crore shareholder or folio accounts.
The seven companies are Tata Steel, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Tata Chemicals, Tata Power, Indian Hotels, Tata Consumer Products and Tata Investment Corporation.

stories.headline: Karnataka bandh called by sugarcane farmers hits Belagavi, but neighbouring districts unaffected
stories.title: Karnataka bandh called by sugarcane farmers hits Belagavi, but neighbouring districts unaffected
stories.summary: Farmers blocked roads at several locations across the district as part of the protest, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appeals to abide by understanding reached at the meeting on October 26
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Normal activities came to a halt in several towns and hobli centres in Belagavi district on October 31 in response to the Karnataka bandh called by sugarcane growers who are demanding a price of ₹5,500 per tonne.
Protesting farmers briefly prevented buses from leaving the Central Bus Stand in Belagavi.
A scuffle broke out between the protesters and the police when the latter attempted to stop them.
The farmers later gathered in front of the Tourist Bungalow and raised slogans against the Union and State governments, reiterating their demand for a higher price for sugarcane.
Several shops were reportedly closed during the protest.
Commercial activity remained largely suspended in Hukkeri, Raibag, Mudalagi, Athani, Nipani, and Chikkodi taluk headquarters, besides several hobli centres.
Farmers blocked roads at several locations across the district as part of the protest.
Among other people, devotees were inconvenienced by the closure of routes leading to temples.
In Dharwad, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Haveri, and Gadag districts, the protests were largely symbolic.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appealed to sugarcane farmers protesting over prices to abide by the understanding reached at the meeting on October 26.
Appealing for calm and patience, Mr. Shivakumar said that sugar factories cannot afford higher procurement prices without a revision in sugar price by the Union Government.
He said that he has reached out to the Prime Minister’s Office for an early decision.
